DeshDash v2

Build state-wise choropleth maps of India — labels, legends, and export in one tool

❓ Help
⚠ Needs one row per state, already aggregated. DeshDash plots what you give it — it doesn't sum, average, or merge duplicate rows for you. If your source has multiple rows per state (e.g. district-level data), combine them first.
State Data
State / UT Value Value Y
?Accepted formats: comma-separated State,Value or tab-separated (paste directly from Excel).
State names: full names (Maharashtra) or 2-letter codes (MH, MP, WB…).
Header row: auto-detected and skipped.
Numbers: commas in numbers are fine — 1,00,000 or 12,500 both work.
?If your file has more than one value column, switch Value column anytime to redraw the map with a different metric — no need to re-upload.
?Works with any CSV — a simple two-column file (state, value) or a wide sheet with extra columns (population, growth rate, literacy rate, etc). Columns are auto-detected and pre-selected in the dropdowns above; confirm or change them, then click Load. If there are several numeric columns, switch between them anytime without re-uploading.
Value Format
?Bivariate combines two independent metrics — name and format each one on its own, since e.g. "Literacy %" and "Population (Cr)" need different units.
Thousands separator (,)
Annotations Data
State / UT Group Note (**bold**, *italic*, __underline__, # heading, - bullet)
?Group is optional — give two or more states the same Group name to color them alike (Style tab → Annotation Fill → Categorical). Each state with text gets a draggable note box near its centroid, auto-shifted to avoid overlaps. Click the ⤢ button on a row to edit its note in a bigger box.
?Format: comma-separated State,Note text or tab-separated (paste directly from Excel).
State names: full names (Maharashtra) or 2-letter codes (MH, MP, WB…).
Line breaks inside a note: type \n where you want a new line.
Header row: auto-detected and skipped. Group isn't set by import — add it in the Table view afterward if needed.
?Columns are auto-detected and pre-selected below; confirm or change them, then click Load. Use \n inside a cell for a line break. Group isn't set by import.

Bivariate Grid & Colors
?Four corner colors, blended across the grid. Low X / Low Y is the base; each axis blends toward its own "high" corner. Picking any preset fills the pickers below — edit them afterward to make a custom palette.
Categorical Colors
Grouped/rare categories
?Some palettes' last color is a similar gray to the default here — if the two look too close together in the legend, change one of them.
?Type a category per state in the Data tab (e.g. dominant crop, scheme type, region class). The categories covering the most states keep their own color, up to the limit above; rarer ones share a gray "Other" swatch — the legend tells you how many states that covers, not how many category names got merged.

Why the dropdown stops at 8: each palette (Set2/Dark2/Paired/Pastel2) ships exactly 8 distinguishable hues. Choosing a higher limit isn't possible here — it would force two "kept" categories to silently reuse the same color, which defeats the purpose of keeping them separate.
